findings.title: The GET unsubscribe endpoint is vulnerable to cross-site request forgery
findings.body: `unsubscribe` changes the current user's notification level during a GET request, and the action is explicitly exempted from `check_xhr`. The URL contains only a publicly discoverable topic slug/id, so another site can navigate an authenticated user's browser to `/t/<slug>/<id>/unsubscribe` and silently downgrade or mute that user's subscription. Keep GET non-mutating and require a CSRF-protected POST after a confirmation, or validate a user-bound signed unsubscribe token.

findings.title: Opening an unsubscribe URL without an existing TopicUser record raises a 500
findings.body: This action assumes every logged-in viewer has a `topic_users` row. A user can directly open the canonical unsubscribe URL for a public topic they have never visited or otherwise been associated with; `TopicUser.find_by` then returns nil and line 107 dereferences `tu.notification_level`, causing `NoMethodError`. Handle the missing row by choosing the appropriate default level and using an upsert such as `TopicUser.change`.

findings.title: Directly saving TopicUser does not record a manual notification override
findings.body: The action assigns and saves `notification_level` directly instead of going through `TopicUser.change`. Consequently `notifications_changed_at` and `notifications_reason_id` are not set to the manual-change values. In particular, a row with a nil reason remains eligible for the automatic tracking logic in `update_last_read`/`auto_track`, which can later promote a user who unsubscribed back to tracking and re-enable topic notifications. This also bypasses the MessageBus notification used to update other open clients. Use `TopicUser.change` (or preserve its metadata and publish behavior) for this update.

findings.title: The added unsubscribe URL is not actually asserted in generated email content
findings.body: The modified test supplies `unsubscribe_url` but still only checks for the pre-existing user-preferences URL. There is no assertion that the per-topic URL appears in the text or HTML email, nor a request/controller test for the notification-level transition. The primary feature can therefore regress or render a broken topic-unsubscribe link without this test failing.
